subject: Biology
prompt: The region of stem where leaves arise is called:

subject: Biology

subject: Biology

explain: Pneumatophores (breathing roots) in mangroves like Rhizophora help in gaseous exchange.

subject: Biology
prompt: Tendrils of Cucumber are modifications of:

subject: Biology

subject: Biology
prompt: The edible part of sweet potato is a modified:

subject: Biology
prompt: A leaf with leaflets attached to a common rachis is:

subject: Biology

explain: Dicots show reticulate venation (network of veins); monocots show parallel venation.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is an example of pinnately compound leaf?
explain: Neem has pinnately compound leaves; Silk cotton and Papaya have palmately compound leaves.

subject: Biology
prompt: The floral formula 'K' stands for:
explain: In floral formula, K = Calyx (sepals), C = Corolla, A = Androecium, G = Gynoecium.

subject: Biology
prompt: Superior ovary is described as:
explain: Hypogynous flower has a superior ovary with thalamus below ovary; e.g., Mustard, Brinjal.

subject: Biology
prompt: Inferior ovary occurs in which floral condition?
explain: Epigynous flowers have inferior ovary with thalamus fused over it; e.g., Cucumber, Guava.

subject: Biology
prompt: Placentation in which ovules are on inner wall of ovary:
explain: Parietal placentation: ovules develop on inner wall of unilocular ovary; e.g., Mustard, Papaya.

subject: Biology
prompt: Marginal placentation is seen in family:
explain: Fabaceae (legumes) show marginal placentation; ovules on margin of monocarpellary ovary.

subject: Biology
prompt: In axile placentation, ovules are attached to:
explain: Axile placentation: ovules on central axis of multilocular ovary; e.g., Tomato, Lemon.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which inflorescence has a fleshy axis with unisexual flowers?
explain: Spadix has a fleshy rachis bearing unisexual sessile flowers enclosed in a spathe; e.g., Colocasia.

subject: Biology
prompt: The fruit of Fabaceae is called:
explain: Fabaceae fruits are legumes (pods), dehiscing along both sutures; e.g., Pea, Bean.

subject: Biology
prompt: Epipetalous stamens are found in:
explain: Solanaceae has epipetalous stamens (stamens attached to petals); e.g., Potato, Tomato.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which family shows zygomorphic flowers and diadelphous stamens?
explain: Fabaceae: zygomorphic flowers, diadelphous stamens (9+1), papilionaceous corolla.

subject: Biology
prompt: Actinomorphic flower can be divided into equal halves by:
explain: Actinomorphic (radial symmetry) flowers can be divided into equal halves by any vertical plane.

subject: Biology
prompt: The edible part of onion is a:
explain: Onion is a bulb — a condensed disc-like stem with fleshy scale leaves; a stem modification.

subject: Biology
prompt: Stipules are found at the base of:
explain: Stipules are leaf-like appendages found at the base of the petiole in many plants.

subject: Biology
prompt: Cymose inflorescence has the main axis that:
explain: In cymose inflorescence, the main axis terminates in a flower, limiting its growth.

subject: Biology
prompt: Prop roots that hang from branches are seen in:
explain: Banyan (Ficus benghalensis) has prop roots hanging from branches giving support.

subject: Biology
prompt: Capitulum (head) inflorescence is characteristic of family:
explain: Asteraceae (Compositae) has capitulum inflorescence with ray and disc florets; e.g., Sunflower.

subject: Biology
prompt: Rhizome is a modified underground stem seen in:
explain: Ginger has a rhizome – a horizontal underground stem with nodes, internodes and scale leaves.

subject: Biology
prompt: Corm is a modified underground stem found in:
explain: Colocasia (taro) has a corm – a condensed, solid, vertical underground stem with stored food.

subject: Biology
prompt: Bulb is a modification of which plant organ?
explain: Bulb (e.g., onion) is a modified compressed stem surrounded by fleshy scale leaves.

subject: Biology
prompt: Runners are stolons that grow along the soil surface in:
explain: Grass produces runners – slender, prostrate stems that creep on the soil surface.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which plant has thorns that are modified stems?
explain: Citrus has stem thorns (modified axillary buds/stems), unlike Rose which has prickles (epidermal outgrowths).

subject: Biology
prompt: Edible part of carrot is a modified:
explain: Carrot is a conical tap root modified for food storage (fusiform in radish, napiform in turnip).

subject: Biology
prompt: Stilt roots seen in Maize are modified:
explain: Maize develops adventitious stilt roots from lower nodes for mechanical support.

subject: Biology
prompt: Leaves modified into spines for protection are seen in:
explain: In Opuntia, leaves are modified into spines to reduce transpiration and provide protection.

subject: Biology
prompt: Leaf tendrils for climbing are seen in:
explain: In Pea, the terminal leaflets of the compound leaf are modified into tendrils for climbing.

subject: Biology
prompt: Parallel venation is characteristic of which plant group?
explain: Monocot leaves show parallel venation where veins run parallel to the midrib.

subject: Biology
prompt: A leaf having the lamina entire/not divided into leaflets is:
explain: A simple leaf has an undivided lamina; incisions if any do not reach the midrib.

subject: Biology
prompt: Palmately compound leaf has leaflets attached at:
explain: In palmate compound leaf, leaflets arise from a single point at the tip of the petiole.

subject: Biology
prompt: Phyllode is a modification of which part of the leaf?
explain: In Australian Acacia, the petiole becomes flat and leaf-like (phyllode) performing photosynthesis.

subject: Biology
prompt: Alternate phyllotaxy is seen in:
explain: China rose (Hibiscus) shows alternate phyllotaxy – one leaf per node on alternate sides.

subject: Biology
prompt: Opposite phyllotaxy where pairs alternate at right angles is called:
explain: Decussate is opposite phyllotaxy where successive pairs of leaves are at 90° to each other.

subject: Biology
prompt: Calyx and corolla together are called:
explain: When calyx and corolla are similar and indistinguishable (as in lily), they are called perianth (tepals).

subject: Biology
prompt: Gamopetalous condition means petals are:
explain: Gamopetalous = fused petals; e.g., Datura. Polypetalous = free petals; e.g., Rose.

subject: Biology
prompt: Epiphyllous stamens are found when stamens are attached to:
explain: In flowers with perianth (monocots like lily), stamens attached to tepals are epiphyllous.

subject: Biology
prompt: Monadelphous condition in stamens means filaments united into:
explain: Monadelphous – all filaments fused into one bundle; e.g., China rose (Hibiscus).

subject: Biology
prompt: Polyadelphous stamens with filaments in many bundles seen in:
explain: Citrus shows polyadelphous stamens where filaments are united into several bundles.

subject: Biology
prompt: Parietal placentation is found in family:
explain: In Mustard (Brassicaceae), ovules are borne on inner wall/outgrowths of the wall – parietal placentation.

subject: Biology
prompt: Basal placentation: ovule is attached at the base of ovary. Example:
explain: In Sunflower (Asteraceae), a single basal ovule is attached at the base of the unilocular ovary.

subject: Biology
prompt: Free central placentation lacks:
explain: Free central placentation – ovules on a central column in unilocular ovary with no septa; e.g., Dianthus.

subject: Biology
prompt: Spike inflorescence has flowers that are:
explain: Spike – racemose inflorescence with sessile (stalkless) flowers on an elongated unbranched axis.

subject: Biology
prompt: Solanaceae family is characterised by floral formula with:
explain: Solanaceae: actinomorphic, K₅ C(5) A₅, bicarpellary syncarpous superior ovary with axile placentation.

subject: Biology
prompt: Fibrous root system is characteristic of:
explain: Monocots have fibrous (adventitious) root systems replacing the primary root early in development.

subject: Biology
prompt: Velamen tissue is found in roots of:
explain: Orchid aerial roots have multilayered velamen for absorbing atmospheric moisture.

subject: Biology
prompt: Edible part of radish is a modified:
explain: Radish is a fusiform modified tap root storing food, making the root the edible part.

subject: Biology
prompt: The underground stem that bears scaly leaves and buds is a:
explain: Rhizome is a modified underground stem with nodes, internodes, scaly leaves and axillary buds.

subject: Biology
prompt: Tendrils of Pisum sativum (pea) are modifications of:
explain: In pea, terminal leaflets of the pinnately compound leaf are modified into tendrils for climbing.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which is an example of unipinnate compound leaf?
explain: Rose has a once-pinnate (unipinnate) compound leaf with leaflets on either side of a single rachis.

subject: Biology
prompt: Whorled phyllotaxy has how many leaves per node?
explain: In whorled phyllotaxy, three or more leaves arise at each node forming a whorl.

subject: Biology
prompt: In floral formula, 'G' with a line above it denotes:
explain: A line drawn above G (Ḡ) in floral formula indicates inferior ovary (epigynous flower).

subject: Biology
prompt: Bicarpellary syncarpous ovary is characteristic of family:
explain: Solanaceae has bicarpellary, syncarpous, bilocular ovary with axile placentation.

subject: Biology
prompt: Corymb inflorescence has flowers that reach the same level because:
explain: In corymb, lower flowers have longer pedicels so all flowers reach the same height (flat top).

subject: Biology
prompt: Umbel inflorescence has all pedicels arising from:
explain: In umbel, all flower stalks (pedicels) arise from a common point, giving an umbrella-like shape.

subject: Biology
prompt: True fruit develops only from:
explain: True (simple) fruit develops solely from the ovary after fertilisation, without other floral parts.

subject: Biology
prompt: Apple is a false fruit because it develops from:
explain: In apple (pome), the fleshy edible part develops from the thalamus, not the ovary, making it false fruit.

subject: Biology
prompt: Tetradynamous condition (4 long + 2 short stamens) is seen in:
explain: Brassicaceae (mustard family) has tetradynamous androecium: 4 long and 2 short stamens.

subject: Biology
prompt: Cruciform corolla (4 free petals in cross shape) is seen in family:
explain: Brassicaceae (Cruciferae) has cruciform corolla with 4 free petals arranged like a cross.

subject: Biology
prompt: Papilionaceous corolla has how many petals?
explain: Papilionaceous corolla of Fabaceae has 5 petals: 1 standard, 2 wings, 2 keels (fused).

subject: Biology
prompt: Trimerous flowers (parts in multiples of 3) are typical of:
explain: Monocot flowers are typically trimerous, with floral parts in threes or multiples of three.

subject: Biology
prompt: Hypogeal germination: cotyledons remain below soil. Example:
explain: In maize (monocot), cotyledon stays below soil; bean shows epigeal germination.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which root modification stores food in Asparagus?
explain: Asparagus has fasciculated fleshy/tuberous adventitious roots for food storage.

subject: Biology
prompt: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association of fungi with:
explain: Mycorrhiza is a mutualistic association between fungal hyphae and plant roots.

subject: Biology
prompt: The edible part of ginger is a modified:
explain: Ginger is a rhizome — underground stem with nodes, internodes and scaly leaves.

subject: Biology
prompt: In Opuntia, the flat green photosynthetic stem is called:
explain: Opuntia has phylloclade — a flattened stem modification performing photosynthesis.

subject: Biology
prompt: Stipular tendrils used for climbing are seen in:
explain: Smilax has stipular tendrils; pea has leaflet tendrils; cucumber has stem tendrils.

subject: Biology
prompt: Valvate aestivation means petals/sepals in bud are:
explain: In valvate aestivation, petals/sepals touch at margins without overlapping.

subject: Biology
prompt: Vexillary (papilionaceous) aestivation is characteristic of family:
explain: Vexillary aestivation with standard, wings, keel petals is unique to Fabaceae.

subject: Biology

explain: Hibiscus (Malvaceae) shows twisted aestivation; each petal overlaps the adjacent one.

subject: Biology

explain: Cassia shows imbricate aestivation; two petals outside, two inside, one partly overlapping.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which placentation is found in Dianthus (Caryophyllaceae)?
explain: Free central placentation with no septa is characteristic of Dianthus/Caryophyllaceae.

subject: Biology
prompt: Number of stamens in Fabaceae flowers is typically:
explain: Fabaceae has 10 diadelphous stamens — 9 united + 1 free.

subject: Biology

explain: Vexillum is the large posterior petal; wings are lateral; keel is the fused anterior pair.

subject: Biology

explain: Solanaceae has 5 epipetalous stamens alternating with corolla lobes.

subject: Biology
prompt: A succulent stem that stores water is seen in:
explain: Opuntia has succulent flattened stem (phylloclade) that stores water in xerophytic conditions.

subject: Biology

explain: Guava has inferior ovary; floral parts arise above the ovary — epigynous condition.

subject: Biology
prompt: Sunflower head (capitulum) has two types of florets:
explain: Capitulum in Asteraceae has peripheral ray florets (ligulate) and central disc florets (tubular).

subject: Biology

subject: Biology
prompt: Aggregate fruit develops from a single flower with:
explain: Aggregate fruit (etaerio) forms from apocarpous gynoecium of a single flower, e.g., Magnolia.

subject: Biology
prompt: Which modification of root helps mangrove plants survive in waterlogged soil?
explain: Pneumatophores (respiratory roots) grow vertically upward for gaseous exchange in waterlogged mangrove habitats. (NCERT)

subject: Biology
